item.title: China and Canada sign deal to deepen financial sector ties
item.description: Canada and China have struck an agreement to deepen collaboration across their financial systems as the two countries seek closer economic ties.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: VANCOUVER — Canada and China have struck an agreement to deepen collaboration across their financial systems as the two countries seek closer economic ties. Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne and International Trade Minister Maninder Sidhu hosted He Lifeng, vice-premier of China, in Vancouver over the past two days. After the meetings, Finance Canada released a joint statement saying the two sides agreed to “enhance financial sector co-operation.” That includes granting greater market access for financial services and fostering engagement between Canadian and Chinese regulatory authorities. The statement adds that both sides reaffirmed their support for multilateralism and “a transparent and predictable environment” for trade and investment. The agreement to deepen financial ties comes as Prime Minister Mark Carney is set to visit China later next week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 9, 2026.

item.title: A new deal brings together two long-life Canadian oilsands and heavy oil companies
item.description: Strathcona Resources Ltd. has signed a deal to buy Greenfire Resources Ltd. in a deal valued at up to $2.9 billion, including debt.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: CALGARY — Strathcona Resources Ltd. has signed a deal to buy Greenfire Resources Ltd. in a deal valued at up to $2.9 billion, including debt. The company says the deal will bring together two long-life oilsands and heavy oil companies. Strathcona says it expects the existing Greenfire leadership team to continue to lead day-to-day operations for the Greenfire assets within a new Strathcona business unit. Under the agreement, Greenfire shareholders may choose to receive either 0.25 of a Strathcona share or $11 in cash for each Greenfire share they hold. Strathcona shares closed at $36.34 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday, while Greenfire shares closed at :$7.93. Strathcona says the Waterous Energy Fund, which holds 72 per cent of Greenfire’s outstanding shares and a 57 per cent stake in Strathcona, has agreed to support the deal and plans to take its payment in shares. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 9, 2026.

item.title: Larry Berman: Will the federal budget help the TSX?
item.description: When you look at the details of Canada’s federal budget as it pertains to investing in Canada, there are aspects that are bullish to be sure. But when you dig down a bit, the largest part of the TSX ...
item.content:encoded:
When you look at the details of Canada’s federal budget as it pertains to investing in Canada, there are aspects that are bullish to be sure. But when you dig down a bit, the largest part of the TSX will face some headwinds with more competition. For banks, this means both opportunities (new market entry, product innovation) and obligations (regulatory compliance, competitive adaptation).

We see the open competition as a slight loss of market share over time, and more of a growth slower than an outright negative. Berman For metals and mining, more support for key minerals should be extremely helpful for growing the sector, but mining is such a highly cyclical sector that policy is not strong enough to call it bullish. It will always depend on underlying commodity trends. Oil and gas stocks are about commodity prices too. The higher prices post-Iran war helped Canada’s revenue side significantly. The planned projects in the budget, if all executed, probably hold the best opportunities, but again, like the war increased revenues, peace will likely reduce them. Growing the sector has regulatory headwinds. Real-time TSX market updates here The software sector is basically two stocks and there is no exchange-traded fund (ETF) for it. Insurance rolls up into financials and there was not much in the budget that we noticed. Summing it up from an ETF perspective, I’ve identified a few ETFs for investors to gain exposure: XFN, XEG, XBM, XGD, and XUT. Berman The worst performing one in the past few years has been utilities. For the yield seekers out there, it might be one of the better performers over the next few years.
